raw_context.item_title: Resolution 26-R-081: Authorizing a Notice of Intention to Issue Sewer Revenue Bonds
raw_context.text: To align with the Capital Improvements Plan (CIP), the City needs to issue debt to finance essential sewer-system improvements. The resolution authorizes a Notice of Intention to issue sewer revenue bonds in an amount not to exceed $42,000,000 in net proceeds, with a principal cap of $43,500,000. The bonds are to be repaid solely from sewer system revenues and are not a general obligation of the City. Current recommended projects under this authorization: Riverside Trunk-Line Rehabilitation: $18,400,000; North Lift-Station Replacement: $9,250,000; Treatment-Plant Capacity Upgrade: $11,100,000; Engineering, contingency, and issuance costs: $3,250,000. Estimated annual debt service is $3,180,000 over a 20-year term.

sources.name: Ordinance 26-O-014 — Animal Control Ordinance (Third Reading), staff report
sources.retrieved_text_or_snapshot: The purpose of the proposed ordinance change is to define the number of dogs and cats a resident may own, to establish guidelines to allow a trap-neuter-release (TNR) program in the community, and to make corrections to the dangerous-dog section of the animal ordinance. The Code Enforcement Division has seen an increasing number of cat hoarding cases. In the past 18 months, Community Service Officers have handled 4 cases involving cat hoarding and have removed 96 cats. The proposed ordinance limits the number of cats and dogs a person may own to six, with no more than four being dogs. This is the third and final reading. The ordinance amends Lakemont Municipal Code Chapter 6, Article II, Section 6-14 (Keeping of Animals) and adds a new Section 6-19 (Trap-Neuter-Release Program). The Public Safety Committee voted 4-1-0 to recommend passage, with Member Holloway dissenting. Staff recommends approval of Ordinance 26-O-014 on third reading.
